item.meaning: The philosophical principle of absolute non-violence toward all living beings, central to Jainism and Buddhism.

item.title: Ethical Frameworks of Ancient Philosophies
item.explanation: Vedic Upaniṣhads, Buddhism, and Jainism emphasized ethical living, self-inquiry, interconnectedness, and Ahiṃsā (non-violence) as core spiritual values.

item.name: Vardhamāna Mahāvīra
item.role_or_contribution: The 24th Tīrthaṅkara of Jainism who revitalized Jain teachings, emphasizing non-violence (Ahiṃsā), truth, and self-restraint.

item.name: Gautama Buddha
item.role_or_contribution: Founder of Buddhism who taught the Four Noble Truths and Eightfold Path to alleviate human suffering.

item.description: The ancient practice of memorizing and transmitting texts like the Vedas orally across generations with strict phonetic precision.
Ancient philosophical dialogues seeking spiritual inquiry into the ultimate reality (Brahman) and individual self (Ātman).
